patch.sql:
with items as (
    select
        order_key,
        count(*) as item_count,
        sum(extended_price) as gross_revenue,
        sum(net_revenue) as net_revenue
    from {{ ref('fct_order_items') }}
    group by order_key
)

select
    o.order_key,
    o.customer_key,
    c.region_name,
    o.order_status,
    o.order_date,
    o.priority,
    coalesce(i.item_count, 0) as item_count,
    coalesce(i.gross_revenue, 0) as gross_revenue,
    coalesce(i.net_revenue, 0) as net_revenue,
    o.loaded_at
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o
-- Fixed join condition: match orders to customers on customer_key, not order_key
left join {{ ref('dim_customers') }} c on o.customer_key = c.customer_key
left join items i on o.order_key = i.order_key
patch.explanation: The original model joined `stg_orders` to `dim_customers` using `o.order_key = c.customer_key`, which mismatched keys and caused `region_name` to be null for most rows, failing the not_null test. Updated the join to correctly use `o.customer_key = c.customer_key`. All other columns, types, and logic remain unchanged.

Join result shows only 375 matches, leaving region_name null for the rest. Upstream tables raw.orders, stg_orders, dim_customers have correct data and no null region_name. The problem originates in the fct_orders model code; fixing the join to `on o.customer_key = c.customer_key` will resolve.
